newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Islamic bank approves $168.5 mln in financing.
newsitem.headline: Islamic bank approves $168.5 mln in financing.

text.p: The Islamic Development Bank (IDB) said on Wednesday it agreed to extend $168.5 million in financing facilities to member states.
An IDB statement said the bank had approved six development projects worth $90 million and three foreign trade operations worth $78.5 million.
Morocco will get $30 million to finance the import of coal, Turkey will receive $25 million to import iron and Algeria will get $23.5 million for the import of spare parts and wires.
The Jeddah-based bank said Libya will get a $28.1 million loan to finance the building of a seaport. It will be repaid after 12 years including a three-year grace period.
Sudan will receive a $22 million loan to finance a water and power project. The loan is repayable in 25 years including a seven-year grace period.
The IDB said it would extend a $18.4 million loan to Qatar to finance the building of a housing complex. It will be repaid in 15 years including a two-year grace period.
It said Cameroon will get a $8.1 million loan to finance a water project, Indonesia a $6.9 million loan and Albania a $6.5 million loan for agricultural projects.

The bank, set up in 1975 to promote trade exchanges between Islamic states, also said it would grant Yemen $4 million in emergency relief to help rebuild schools and health centres damaged in recent floods.
